2) Average response length in characters (you said ~3,800 chars)
3) Average requests per active user per day (you said ~3)
4) Monthly active users (ballpark) — we'll run examples for 10k and 50k below if you don't have a firm number.

Quick note about next steps: once you confirm, Grace (solutions engineer) can produce a short worksheet with token conversions and a 3-tier cost projection (conservative / expected / optimistic) that shows what $/1M token pricing would mean for the scenarios. Also would be useful if you can attach a 24–48h sample of raw requests (anonymized) — that'll let us estimate cache hit opportunities.

Our questions inline are small and intended to remove ambiguity so we don't under/over-index pricing. Thanks — I looped in Avery for contract/discount questions.

Subject: Re: Clarifying billing units (tokens vs chars vs requests) + cache impact — post-call

Hi Alice —

Thanks for confirming and for the sample. Below is a pragmatic, conservative conversion and a worked example so you have a baseline to pass to finance. Grace and I will follow up with a small spreadsheet and a short call to walk through.

Short answers:
- Conversion (rule of thumb): roughly 3.5–4.3 characters per token depending on language and punctuation; we use 4 chars/token for conservative modeling unless you want us to tokenize your sample precisely.
- Billing: Redwood primarily charges based on tokens (prompt tokens + generated/output tokens). There are no additional per-request fees on our standard hosted plans; requests only matter for performance and rate limits.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching can reduce billed tokens when identical prompt+context would produce the same completion. Dynamic user-specific fields (user_id, session_id, timestamps) do reduce cache effectiveness. Common mitigation: replace high-variance fields with placeholders (e.g., "{USER_ID}") prior to the call so that the model sees the same prefix and cache hits become possible. We can help instrument that approach.

Worked example (conservative assumptions):
- Use 4 chars/token
- Prompt: 1,200 chars -> 300 tokens
- Response: 3,800 chars -> 950 tokens
- Total per request: 1,250 tokens (prompt + output)
- Requests per DAU/day: 3 -> tokens/DAU/day = 3 * 1,250 = 3,750 tokens
- For 10,000 DAU: 3,750 * 10,000 = 37,500,000 tokens/day -> ~37.5M/day
- Monthly (30 days): ~1,125,000,000 tokens = 1,125 million tokens

Cost at various $/1M-token rates (monthly):
- $8 / 1M tokens -> 1,125 * $8 = $9,000 / month
- $10 / 1M tokens -> 1,125 * $10 = $11,250 / month
- $12 / 1M tokens -> 1,125 * $12 = $13,500 / month

Notes:
- Those numbers assume zero cache hits. If you can normalize prompts to get even modest cache hits (e.g., 10–30% of requests), that directly reduces billed tokens in the same proportion. Example: 20% cache hit reduces billed tokens to ~900M -> cost at $10/1M drops to ~$9,000/mo.
- If responses are deterministic or you can precompute frequent completions and serve from a cache/lookup table, effective cost can be much lower.
- For a 50k DAU scenario multiply the 10k numbers by 5 (so ~5.625B tokens/month).

Next steps we propose: 
1) Grace will run your attached sample through our tokenizer and produce an exact token conversion + a small pivot table (conservative/expected/optimistic) — delivery EOD tomorrow.
2) If you'd like, we can run a 2-week pilot (instrumentation + pilot traffic) to measure real-world token footprint and cache hit rate; we can cap spend for the pilot so it's safe for procurement.
3) Avery will outline discount thresholds for reserved capacity / committed volume and a 1M-token target pricing cadence (e.g., tiered discounts at 1B / 3B / 10B/mo).

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk the numbers with Finance & Engineering?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
